rationale: Lyc. reflex of ϭⲟⲗ 'lie, falsehood.' Distinct from glossary ⲡⲁ̄ⲗⲁⲍ 'strife.' Heads vice-catalogue paired with ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲙⲛⲧⲣⲉ ⲛⲛⲟⲩⲭ 'false witness of falsehood.'
Compound: ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲙⲛⲧⲣⲉ ('state-of-witnessing') + ⲛ̄ⲛⲟⲩⲭ ('of falsehood'). Standard biblical-legal sin (cf. Decalogue 'false witness'). The doubled abstract ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲙⲛⲧⲣⲉ marks the perjury-act as such.
Greek loanword καταλαλιά 'evil speech, slander.' Standard NT/early Christian moral term (cf. 1 Pet 2:1, 2 Cor 12:20).
Greek loanword κατηγορία 'accusation, indictment.' Pairs with καταλαλιά in legal-moral register.
Greek loanword μαγεία/μαγία 'magic, sorcery.' Standard sin-catalogue term (cf. Gal 5:20 φαρμακεία).
Lexeme of uncertain identification. Position in vice-catalogue between ⲙⲁⲅⲓⲁ and 'consuming fire' suggests a magical-malevolent term. Possibly Lyc. for ϩⲁⲣⲉ/ϣⲁⲩⲣⲉ (curse/spell). Confidence low.
Compound: ⲥⲉⲧⲉ ('fire') + ⲣⲉϩ-ⲟⲩⲱⲙ ('one-who-eats/devours'). 'Devouring fire' as image of destructive passion or punitive judgment-fire.
Standard Coptic ⲥⲓⲧⲉ/ⲥⲱⲧⲉ 'seed.' Here used in moral-anatomical register: 'the seed which exists in the body of man' = the seed of evil/passion.
Lyc. ⲍⲁⲗⲉ = ϩⲁⲗⲉ 'poison, venom' (with regular ⲍ for ϩ). The seed acts within the body 'like a poison.'
Greek loanword πορνεία. Standard NT/early Christian moral term.
Lyc. reflex of ⲃⲗ̄ⲗⲉ 'be blind.' Translated 'in which a man is blinded' — fornication blinds the moral perception. Alternative reading from ⲃⲱⲗ family ('be loosed') is possible.
Standard Coptic ⲧⲏⲩ 'wind, breath, spirit.' In moral-anthropological context here = the agitating impulse of desire that gives the man no rest.
Aramaic loan via Greek μαμωνᾶς (cf. Matt 6:24, Luke 16:9-13). Capitalized as personified cosmic principle of greed.
Privative abstract: ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲁⲧ- ('un-') + ⲥⲓ ('be filled, satisfied'). The state of never-being-filled — characteristic of greed/Mammon.
Already in glossary as ⲡⲁⲍⲉ 'lifespan' (Lyc. ⲍ for ϩ in ⲁϩⲉ). Confirmed here in possessive form: 'all his lifespan he is not satisfied.'
ⲡⲛⲁ̄ = standard Coptic abbreviation of πνεῦμα; ⲉⲧⲍⲁⲩ = Lyc. qualitative 'evil' (= Sah. ⲉⲧϩⲟⲟⲩ). Standard Manichaean term for the demonic spiritual principle whose works manifest as catalogued sins.
Greek loanword βασανίζω 'torment, examine under torture.' Standard Coptic borrowing.
Lyc. possessive substantival 'mine' (= Sah. ⲛⲟⲩⲓ̈). The personified-evil voice protests: 'if they are mine, you do them.'
Lyc. ⲭ for ϫ; = ϫⲓ-ⲟⲩⲁ 'utter blasphemy/insult.' Same root as ⲣⲉϩⲭⲓⲟⲩⲁ 'blasphemer' in glossary. Used here in future relative: 'you who shall blaspheme against God.'
Greek loanword κελεύω 'command' with verbalizing ⲣ̄- prefix. Standard Coptic + Greek-loan composite.
Lyc. variant of ⲟⲩⲱⲥϩ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ in glossary 'cut away, reap out.' Here the action is the moral 'reaping' of consequences from the evil deeds.
Standard Manichaean Christological designation; the Father acts 'through his beloved Son' in the apostolic mission. Cf. Matt 3:17 / Mark 1:11 dominical formula.
